issues.summary: poses-map batch authoring produced FOUR IDENTICAL keyframes (the rig's pre-existing 37/31deg pose) across four different requested keyposes while reporting "3 joint(s) posed" — an honesty bug: posing silently failed but the tool claimed success. Two confirmed aggravators: (1) STALE PLAYING AnimationTracks hijack every StepAnimations call and re-stamp their pose over the batch's (fixed by stopping tracks — but the tool must detect/refuse this itself); (2) even after stopping tracks + resetting Transforms on a grip_tool-held rig the snapshot still captured the old pose — suspect the batch applies rotations to a channel (Transform) the snapshot does not read on held rigs (C0-based arm-hold), or the apply is undone before snapshot.
issues.repro: workspace.AgentRig with grip_tool-equipped Sword (AgentEditGrip present) after several Animator preview tracks were played: add_keyframe {clip:"SwordUse", poses:{RightShoulder:{x:-160,z:25},RightElbow:{x:40},AgentEditGrip:{x:30}}} x4 with different values -> dump keyframe poses -> all identical RightUpperArm=37 RightLowerArm=31. Reproduced post-reload and post-track-stop+Transform-reset.
issues.resolution: PENDING - (a) batch must VERIFY the applied pose survived to snapshot time (read back the joint rotation after apply; error loudly on mismatch instead of keying a lie); (b) refuse/stop-and-warn when the Animator has playing tracks; (c) resolve the Transform-vs-C0 snapshot channel question for grip-held rigs. The single-call pose_joint path and the earlier clean-rig batch verify (BatchTest 40deg stored) both worked - the failure needs the held-rig + track-history state.

issues.summary: grip_tool writes the arm-hold pose into joint C0 (RightShoulder ~37deg / RightElbow ~31deg) and NOTHING restores it when the Tool is unequipped/reparented away - the rig keeps the bent holding-arm pose forever (user screenshot: rig at rest with arm across chest, blade crossing the body). The residue also contaminates keypose authoring snapshots and made a grip look correct in preview while wrong at true neutral.

issues.title: trellis.generate has no starvation detection or result salvage: a VRAM-starved NVIDIA run computes 15-20x slow into a client timeout, and the finished GLB is discarded (dead socket)
issues.symptom: forge-falchion 2026-07-16: res-1024 AND res-512 (measured-87s config) both ran past the 1200s client timeout at 82-91% GPU util with 7.1/8.2GB VRAM used (Studio + desktop tenants); two server jobs completed into dead sockets, zero GLBs landed, ~45 min wasted. Recovery that worked: kill trellis-server, relaunch with STUDIO_AGENT_TRELLIS_VK_DEVICES='' (the 33GB AMD iGPU lane), regenerate.
issues.repro: fill NVIDIA VRAM to ~7GB (Studio open + browser/streaming tenants), trellis.generate(resolution=512) -> observe wall >> 87s norm and eventual urllib timeout while nvidia-smi shows high util
issues.resolution: PENDING - driver should (a) measure wall-vs-norm and surface a starvation warning naming the iGPU lane, (b) auto-fall-back to VK_DEVICES='' on a starved timeout, (c) ideally the server writes the GLB to disk so a client timeout does not orphan finished compute (needs a trellis.cpp flag probe).

issues.title: ORACLE BUG: played_arc_of twin cannot resolve the equipped Tool's Handle under the rig (clip_arc_of twin stays pending)
issues.symptom: play oracle played_arc_of {rig:'Workspace.AgentRig', clip:'SwordSlash'} -> UNKNOWN 'tracked part Handle not found under rig' while the rig demonstrably holds the equipped ForgeLongsword (Handle present, edit-side clip_arc_of PASSes 91.9 deg on the same clip). The melee suite therefore can never fully green a held weapon: clip_arc_of's EDIT_MISLEADS pass stays twin_pending.
issues.repro: Equip a stamped Tool on workspace.AgentRig (grip_tool), play start, then `play oracle {check:'played_arc_of', args:{rig:'Workspace.AgentRig', clip:'SwordSlash'}}`
issues.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 - FindFirstChild('Handle', true) was returning a POSE instance: the rig's AnimSaves clips carry weapon-channel Pose objects NAMED 'Handle', and the recursive search matched one before the real part (not a BasePart -> 'not found'). The census never tripped because it resolves a full PATH. Fix: walk GetDescendants, BaseParts only (src/PlayBridge.luau, 6b51f11). Live-verified: tracked Workspace.AgentRig.ForgeLongsword.Handle, full-clip runtime playback, sweep 124.2 deg over 600 samples; the melee suite then hit its FIRST green=true (14/0/0, both twins sidecar-witnessed, session 6).

issues.title: ORACLE BUG: clip_self_intersect - suite vs capture disagree (weapon-sword)
issues.symptom: suite said: PASS with blade_in_body_max=0 studs, but reports blade_in_arm_max_studs=0.4392 against its own stated max_allowed_depth=0.2 | capture showed: Front strip t=0.56 and left strip t=0.42 show the blade grazing/overlapping the right forearm; the check reports an arm threshold it never enforces, so a 2.2x-over-allowance arm penetration passes sil
issues.repro: oracle_suite on game.StarterPack.ForgeArmingSword vs a full capture review (audit run, rung weapon-sword)
issues.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 - two bugs in one. (a) The arm gate WAS enforced, but at a lazy 1.0-stud default; the 'stated' max_allowed_depth=0.2 sitting beside blade_in_arm_max_studs was actually the OTHER mode's part-AABB gate - a payload-honesty failure that misled the audit (and would mislead any reader). (b) Fix: default max_blade_in_arm 1.0 -> 0.3 (same centerline instrument + gate as max_blade_in_body: one grazing sample of a ~3-stud blade passes, sustained overlap fails), and EVERY printed gate now rides beside its measurement under its exact arg name (max_part_aabb_depth / max_blade_in_arm / max_blade_in_body). Live both-branch verification on the staged sword: default FAILs '0.44 studs of blade centerline INSIDE RightLowerArm at t=0.45 (max 0.3)' - the audit's exact capture-seen overlap; arg max_blade_in_arm=0.6 PASSes the same measurement. Honest suite verdict now 13 PASS / 1 FAIL: the artifact's follow-through flaw stands RECORDED (pose fixup = a separate human call; the staged evidence keeps its integrity). LATER SAME DAY (fleet clip pass): the one-sample allowance made LENGTH-CONSISTENT - default max_blade_in_arm = max(0.3, 1.5 x the declared blade's centerline-sample quantum = len*0.85/12) after the 4.3-stud rapier's single near-hilt sample at the raise (eyes-checked clean) read 0.3046 over the fixed floor; every original 2-sample flaw still fails under the new default. All three fleet clips then pose-fixed via ramped grip-channel corrections: weapon_sword 0.439->0.220 (follow-through cock 45->30 deg, sweep IMPROVED 130->134.8), ForgeLongsword 0.602->0.000 (ramped -25 deg tail), DivineRapier 0.609->0.305-under-quantum-gate (-14 deg envelope thru the salute). Fleet: 15/0/0, 15/0/0, 14/1/0 (the 1 = issue #29's thrust-vs-slash prior).

issues.title: ORACLE BUG: capture framing (suite blindspot) - suite vs capture disagree (weapon-sword)
issues.symptom: suite said: no suite row asserts capture readability | capture showed: capture_angles angle 4/4 (270deg) was fully occluded by the torso and angle 'right' rendered from the Left viewcube, so one of four sign-off angles carried zero information
issues.repro: oracle_suite on game.StarterPack.ForgeArmingSword vs a full capture review (audit run, rung weapon-sword)
issues.resolution: RESOLVED 2026-07-25 - BOTH halves confirmed real, plus a bonus bug the fix exposed. (1) 'right is Left': subject-relative preset yaws were ADDED to the rig's facing, which mirrors handedness (a subject facing the camera has its right on the viewer's left) - empirically proven with a neon marker on the rig's true right: BEFORE shot shows viewcube 'Left' + the L-skinned flank + marker hidden; AFTER (CaptureCore.composeYaw = facing MINUS preset, wired into capture_angles AND capture_animation) shows viewcube 'Right' + R flank + marker foreground. (2) Occluded sign-off angles: NEW check capture_vantage (EDIT_OK, in the melee suite) raycasts from each angle's framed camera to 12 declared-centerline samples; visible_frac under min_visible_frac (0.3) FAILs naming the first blocker. Live both-branch: front/right/left PASS 0.92/0.83/0.83; back FAILs at 0.00 (the audit's zero-information angle, mechanized). (3) BONUS (exposed by suite integration): scrubClip restored Motor6D.Transforms but never re-solved joints, so every check AFTER a clip check measured the LAST SCRUBBED POSE, not rest (the applyPose fact) - fixed with a fresh Animator:StepAnimations(0) after restore. Suite on weapon_sword: 14 PASS / 1 FAIL (only the honest arm graze).
